chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Ajli (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan told us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib told us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlul told us, from his father, from Ali ibn Ghurab, saying: The best of the Ja'fars, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, told me, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family) cursed the namisa, the muntamisa, the washira, the mustawshira, the wasila, the mustawsila, the washima, and the mustawshima.

key_terms.النَّامِصَة: The woman who plucks or removes hair for beautification
key_terms.وَالْمُسْتَوْشِرَة: The woman who has tattoo/ink applied to her
key_terms.وَالْمُسْتَوْصِلَة: The woman who has hair attached/extended to her
key_terms.وَالْمُنْتَمِصَة: The woman who has hair plucked/removed for her

ai.seo_question: What are the eight specific female beauty practices cursed by the Prophet in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith details the Prophet’s curse on eight terms denoting women who alter Allah’s creation through hair plucking, tattooing, and extensions. In Shia scholarship, these practices are viewed as *taghyir khalq Allah* (changing God's creation), with the dual mention of the practitioner and the recipient emphasizing the communal nature of the act. The terms reflect specific pre-Islamic and early Islamic beauty customs that were prohibited to preserve natural dignity.
